reader.decision: Approve removing the digest_builder line from the crontab mirror and ticking the cutover checkbox. The live ops-box-2 crontab gets the same edit. Defer the unique index to a later change.
reader.decision_reason: The message says the duplicates come from two schedulers running the same job, and deleting the stale cron line removes that cause for one line. The index is a useful guard but costs more (ON CONFLICT change and cleanup of existing duplicates). Dedupe by email hides the cause and drops shared-email subscribers.

reconstruction.problem: Since the 21 Sept 2026 Kubernetes cutover, both the ops-box-2 cron and the Kubernetes CronJob run jobs.digest_builder at 06:00 on Mondays. Each run inserts one pending outbox row per active subscriber. The builder does not check for an existing row and outbox has no unique constraint, so every subscriber has two rows.
reconstruction.what_breaks: digest-mailer sends both pending rows, so every subscriber gets the Monday digest twice.
reconstruction.fix: Delete the digest_builder line (line 3) from the ops-box-2 crontab. That means editing the mirror at ops/hosts/ops-box-2/crontab and the live crontab on the host. Also tick the digest_builder checkbox in docs/migrations/2026-09-k8s-cutover.md. Add the unique index on outbox(subscriber_id, digest_date) later.
reconstruction.cost: The crontab fix costs one line and one host edit. The risk is that the Kubernetes job becomes the only run, so a failed pod means no digest. The unique index would need ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in the builder and deletion of existing duplicate rows first.

reader.closing_answer: Yes. Remove the digest_builder line from the crontab mirror and tick the cutover checkbox, and leave the unique index for a later change. The mirror alone changes nothing, so the live crontab on ops-box-2 needs the same edit. Do that too, or tell me who has access to the host.
